sonnet.problem: The question puts a prediction in the present tense: 'The LORD pleads the case of Israel and Judah to bring rest to the earth.' The text says 'He will fervently plead their case so that He may bring rest to the earth.'
sonnet.rule: A prediction stays a prediction: "God says Tyre will fall," never "Tyre falls."

sonnet.problem: The question restates the rhetorical questions ('who is like Him... what shepherd can stand against Him'), and the right answer ('No one can challenge Him') is just those questions turned around ('who can challenge Me?'). The question holds its own answer. The text also never states what the questions make clear.
sonnet.rule: A choice card's question never holds its own answer, or a form of it, like "rock badgers" for "in the rocks." Ask something else.

sonnet.problem: The card says the archers camp around Babylon 'so no one escapes,' which makes the second command the purpose of the first. The text gives two separate commands: 'Encamp all around her; let no one escape.'
sonnet.rule: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.
